episodes.170897: A few strong to marginally severe thunderstorms produced isolated instances of wind damage.

episodes.170913: Isolated thunderstorms developed over much of the area on the afternoon and evening of the 9th.  Dry air beneath the cloud bases led to an evaporatively enhanced downburst directly over the Amherst (Lamb County) mesonet.
episodes.170936: Another active monsoon day was in store for northern and central New Mexico on August 9, 2022. As is typical, thunderstorms first developed over the high terrain areas before becoming more widespread as the day progressed. Some of these thunderstorms were more robust and produced heavy rainfall which led to flash flooding. Most notably for the day, the McBride burn scar near Ruidoso was hit hard with flash flooding. Road closures from debris flow were also reported near Golden.
episodes.171290: Heavy rain across the areas caused localized flooding and a mudslide to occur. In other areas, thunderstorms produced gusty and erratic outflow winds.
episodes.171376: A stationary boundary was draped just north of the Ohio River, which allowed for the development of generally isolated showers and thunderstorms across the state throughout the day. One of these storms developed near the eastern TN border in Whitley County, and eventually was warned. This storm did end up producing an insolated instance of wind damage, with one tree being reported down near the community of Louden.
episodes.171443: Multiple rounds of monsoonal thunderstorms occurred on August 7th through the 9th. A few severe thunderstorms produced high winds, while many others produced very heavy rain and flash flooding.
episodes.171606: Isolated thunderstorms developed into slow-moving clusters of storms during the heat of the afternoon. A couple of storms produced isolated wind damage. A weak cold front trailed southwest along the Ohio Valley from a low pressure system over the northeastern states. The storms developed along this front in a moist and unstable air mass.
episodes.171664: During the evening of the 8th, a surface low developed northeastward in southern Ontario and allowed the trailing cold front to move southeastward from southern Lower Michigan and southwestern Ontario to northwest Ohio and central Lake Erie. Ahead of the front, a line of multicell thunderstorms eventually evolved/persisted southeastward from Lake Erie and generated isolated straight-line wind damage in northeast Ohio. These storms encountered moderate MUCAPE and DCAPE, respectively, and weak to moderate effective bulk shear in the warm sector.
episodes.171878: Afternoon sea breeze thunderstorms produce gusty winds over the coastal waters around west central Florida.
episodes.171917: Thunderstorms moving offshore of the Brevard County coast produced strong wind gusts.
episodes.172176: A drier and more stable prevailing SE flow was over the area in the wake of a departing TUTT. Sea breeze and outflows converged across inland SE GA in the late afternoon and early evening where stronger downdrafts occurred and caused some wind damage due to drier mid level air enhancing DCAPE values.
episodes.172388: On August 9th and 10th, a quasi-stationary surface front meandered along the Ohio River, serving as a focus for the development of daytime showers and thunderstorms. Immediately south of the surface boundary, an unusually moist environment was present, with precipitable water values exceeding 2 inches across central Kentucky. As a result, as modest instability developed during the afternoon hours on the 9th, scattered showers and thunderstorms formed across Kentucky, with one cell growing strong enough to produce isolated wind damage across Trimble County. Then, on the afternoon of August 10th, widespread showers and thunderstorms once again developed across most of central Kentucky, with storms producing heavy rainfall amounts thanks to weak steering flow (slow storm motion) and the aforementioned available moisture. Flash flooding was observed during the afternoon hours across several locations, with the most significant flooding being observed in Franklin County and Casey County.
episodes.172442: Oppressive heat and humidity led to isolated thunderstorms.  One storm in western Massachusetts caused damage due to a lightning strike.
episodes.172443: A cold front moved into a hot and steamy environment to create strong to severe thunderstorms across southeastern MA and eastern RI during the late afternoon and evening.  There was some temporary, but significant, urban flooding.
episodes.172444: A cold front moved into a hot and steamy environment to create strong to severe thunderstorms across southeastern MA and eastern RI during the late afternoon and evening.  There was some temporary, but significant, urban flooding.
episodes.172575: Scattered thunderstorms developed in the afternoon across the Tennessee Valley, with a few producing wind gusts that blew down trees.
episodes.172711: Thunderstorms developed into southeastern Oklahoma during the early morning hours of the 9th, as a cold front moved into the area. The strongest storms produced damaging wind gusts.
episodes.172923: Scattered strong summer storms resulted in gusty winds in excess of 34 knots across portions of the coastal waters.
episodes.173147: Isolated to scattered showers and storms developed during the peak heating of the day. One cluster of these storms grew strong enough to produce damaging wind gusts and quarter size hail.
episodes.173228: A cluster of thunderstorms developed in the evening near the I-70 corridor ahead of a slow moving cold front. These thunderstorms produced heavy rain and isolated flash flooding across southeast Illinois, with some locations observing rainfall rates that exceeded 2 inches per hour. An additional cluster of thunderstorms moved across the same areas early on the morning of August 9th, producing more flooding.
episodes.173235: A weak upper trough shifted southeast into the Red River Valley of Southern Oklahoma and Western Arkansas during the morning of August 9th, which focused concentrated areas of showers and thunderstorms as it encountered a hot, very moist, and unstable air mass. These showers and thunderstorms were slow moving, with widespread 2-4+ inches of rain falling over both the Texas and Arkansas sides of Texarkana, as well as across much of Southwest Arkansas. This resulted in flash flooding across the city of Texarkana, with numerous roads flooded as 3.94 inches of rain fell over the course of a few hours at the Texarkana Regional Airport.
episodes.173236: A weak upper trough shifted southeast into the Red River Valley of Southern Oklahoma and Western Arkansas during the morning of August 9th, which focused concentrated areas of showers and thunderstorms as it encountered a hot, very moist, and unstable air mass. These showers and thunderstorms were slow moving, with widespread 2-4+ inches of rain falling over both the Texas and Arkansas sides of Texarkana, as well as across much of Southwest Arkansas. This resulted in flash flooding across the city of Texarkana, with numerous roads flooded as 3.94 inches of rain fell over the course of a few hours at the Texarkana Regional Airport.
episodes.173257: Aa high pressure circulation centered near the Four Corners allowed deep monsoon moisture to become thoroughly entrenched across northern Arizona. Surface dew points were generally above 60 F south of the Mogollon Rim, with values in the 50s along and north of the Rim.  Precipitable water ranged from 1.0 to 1.75 inches, with the highest values across southern Yavapai County.
episodes.173298: An upper-level trough combined with strong instability (SB CAPE of 2000+ J/KG) and high moisture content (PWAT of 1.7+ inches) to result in the development of strong to severe thunderstorms across portions of Riverside and Imperial Counties during the afternoon and early evening hours. A complex of thunderstorms originating from southwest Arizona moved westward through Riverside while intensifying in the process. Another complex of storms then developed near the international border and affected Imperial County.
episodes.173302: Under a favorable easterly flow, a subtle disturbance in the upper-levels moved across southwest Arizona into southeast California, resulting in diurnally induced thunderstorm activity across the area during the early afternoon hours. High instability (SBCAPE 2000+ J/KG) and very high moisture content (PWAT 2+ inches) resulted in a favorable environment for strong thunderstorms leading to flash flooding to materialize. Flash flooding was reported along several stretches of SR-95 in La Paz County. Radar estimates of 1-3 inches were observed along the area that reported the flooding.
episodes.173406: A southward shift in the Westerlies forced a slow moving front to move southeastward into the Ozarks Region on the 8th. The front then stalled and interacted with several upper level disturbances to produce heavy rainfall and severe storms over the area through the early afternoon of the 9th. The strongest storms occurred during the afternoon and evening of the 9th, producing widespread damaging wind gusts which blew down trees and powerlines, and hail to the size of ping pong balls. The hardest hit areas were along and south of Interstate 44 from Joplin to Springfield to south of Lebanon. Rainfall accumulations of two to over four inches occurred from the Lake of the Ozarks to Stockton Lake and then southward toward Springfield, Mount Vernon and Neosho.
episodes.173409: A ongoing rainy pattern that had been in place for a week or more continued on August 9th. The seabreeze boundary on the south side of Lake Ponchartrain became the focus for thunderstorms to develop around the New Orleans Metro. Due to the fact that these storms developed on the seabreeze, their movement was slow. This, combined with abundant moisture in place, resulted in flash flooding at a few locations in Jefferson Parish.
episodes.173430: A cold front moving through the area forced thunderstorm development late in the day on August 9th. These slow moving thunderstorms developed in an area of 2 to 2.2 inches of precipitable water with CAPE values near 2000 J/kg. These thunderstorms dropped a quick 1 to 1.5 inches of rainfall in less than an hour, producing localized flash flooding.
episodes.173468: A typical summertime pattern prevailed with scattered afternoon thunderstorms across the tri-state region. A few storms produced damaging wind gusts with impacts to trees and power lines.
episodes.173472: Isolated thunderstorms produced localized wind damage at Abilene State Park.
episodes.173478: A typical summertime pattern prevailed with scattered afternoon thunderstorms across the tri-state region. A few storms produced damaging wind gusts with impacts to trees and power lines along with heavy rain which resulted in localized flooding.
episodes.173512: A deep east-southeast monsoon flow brought plenty of Gulf of Mexico moisture into the region. A weak surface low extended through southwest New Mexico which helped to fuel slow moving thunderstorms with heavy rain and flash flooding.
episodes.173513: Deep easterly monsoonal flow had brought plenty of moisture into the Borderland over the previous days.  A severe thunderstorm developed over the Franklin Mountains and headed west through El Paso and Canutillo.
episodes.173527: Heavy rainfall repeatedly moved across portions of Northwestern Alabama, producing nuisance flooding, as well as a few instances of flash flooding (water flooding a basement) just West of Underwood-Petersville. Upwards of three inches of rain fell between 10pm and Midnight in this area.
episodes.173544: Typical afternoon and evening summertime thunderstorms developed on August 6th and August 9th.  Some of the storms were locally strong, producing isolated wind damage across Central Alabama.
episodes.173572: Increasing moisture and instability the night of Aug. 8th and on the 9th resulted in the development of strong thunderstorms capable of strong winds and heavy downpours across portions of central Oregon. These storms were in fact able to produce strong enough winds that brought down trees between Sunriver and La Pine.
episodes.173614: Thunderstorms moved northwest across Cochise, Graham, Pinal and northeast Pima counties during the evening. One storm uprooted a tree in downtown Tucson.
episodes.173617: Thunderstorms moved northwest across southeast Arizona during the afternoon and evening. In Tucson, power poles and trees were downed and some roads were flooded. Flash flooding also occurred in Nogales.
episodes.173659: Scattered thunderstorms developed over northeast Georgia during the afternoon. A couple of severe storms produced brief damaging wind gusts over Rabun County.
episodes.173661: Scattered thunderstorms developed over western North Carolina during the afternoon. One of the storms produced brief damaging wind gusts in Buncombe County.
episodes.173729: A weak trough moved across South Florida and enhanced typical afternoon showers and thunderstorms over the western Florida peninsula and adjacent Gulf waters.
episodes.173745: Scattered storms popped up with daytime heating across much of western and central Oklahoma during the afternoon of the 9th, with large hail and damaging wind gusts accompanying the strongest storms.
episodes.173775: Gale-force wind gusts occurred in association with showers and thunderstorms near the westernmost lower Florida Keys as the northern portion of a tropical wave moved westward through the Straits of Florida.
episodes.173794: Moist southeast flow fueled thunderstorms over southeast California. Several storms produced flash flooding, and a few produced severe weather.
episodes.173795: Moist southeast flow fueled thunderstorms over southern Nevada. Several storms produced severe weather, and a few produced flash flooding.
episodes.177586: Scattered afternoon thunderstorms developed across portions of Mississippi on August 7th and 8th. A few of these storms were severe and produced damaging wind gusts.
episodes.178462: Slow moving afternoon thunderstorms produced heavy rain and flash flooding in parts of southeast Arkansas.
